To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fluxes of the muons of the first and second generations are determined by the fluxes of pions of the first and third generations, respectively.
the fluxes of muons and mesons in the atmosphere can be described by simple analytical formulas that are applicable to all physically relevant values of the zenith angle, energy, and depth.

the muon flux in the atmosphere is determined by the flux of pions, the muon flux is a function of the energy of the muon and of the zenith angle, and the muon flux decreases with increasing energy and zenith angle.

the muon component of cosmic radiation can be considered as a superposition of the following components: (1) the muons produced in the atmosphere by the decay of the charged pions produced in the primary cosmic-ray interactions; (2) the muons generated in the atmosphere by interactions of the primary particles and the decay of the muon produced in the primary interactions; (3) the muons of the primary component of the cosmic radiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the obtained formulas are sufficiently accurate, simple to use, and can be applied for the entire energy region of muon production in cosmic rays.
the formulas obtained in our study can be used to calculate the muon fluxes with an accuracy of 10% for all zenith angles and energies.
we derived a formula for the flux of muons in the atmosphere for all depths (from the top of the atmosphere down to the ground), energies and zenith angles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the muon component of the cosmic radiation is a superposition of two components: a component of the flux of muons produced directly in the atmosphere and a component of the muons produced in the atmosphere by decay of the mesons.

the fluxes of secondary particles are determined by the properties of the primary particle flux and the properties of the atmosphere, and the dependence of the fluxes of the secondary particles on the zenith angle and the energy is determined by the properties (masses, cross sections, lifetimes, decay modes) of the particles involved in the nuclear cascade.

the flux of muons with energy E> 1 GeV is determined by the flux of pions with energy E>1 GeV, while muons with energy 1 GeV<E< 100 GeV are mainly created in interactions of pions and muons with the nuclei in the atmosphere, and the flux of muon neutrinos is mainly determined by the fluxes of muons and neutrinos of all energies.
